Adu218UsbfsLink on real hardware: does the link seam actually work?
==================================================================
Date: 2026-08-25.  Unit: USB 0a07:00da serial E02246, firmware bcdDevice 0000
Host: Arduino Uno Q, user `arduino` (in `dialout`), node /dev/bus/usb/001/015
Code under test: src/benchctrl/drivers/ontrak_adu218/usbfs.py, run unmodified
                 (scp'd to /tmp and imported; no driver layer exists yet)

This is the first execution of any ADU218 PRODUCTION code. Everything before
it was throwaway probe scripts in /tmp. So the question is narrow: does the
module -- ioctl constants derived rather than hardcoded, framing, timeouts,
lifecycle -- behave the way the probe scripts did?

Section G below is the one that matters, and it is deliberately WEAK: RPK0 is
the ADU218's own report of its own state. A link that mangled a command
identically in both directions would pass it. The independent witness is in
link_dmm_witness.txt.

== A. find_device by serial ==
   Adu218Device(path='/dev/bus/usb/001/015', bus=1, device=15, serial='E02246')
== B. open / claim / drain ==
   is_open before: False
   is_open after : True
   repr          : Adu218UsbfsLink(serial='E02246', timeout_ms=200, open=True)
   device        : E02246 /dev/bus/usb/001/015
== C. reads (no state change) ==
   PK    -> '000'         ( 11.75 ms)
   RPK0  -> '0'           ( 16.17 ms)
   RPA   -> '0000'        ( 15.73 ms)
   RPB   -> '0000'        ( 15.94 ms)
   DB    -> '1'           ( 16.02 ms)
   WD    -> '0'           ( 15.83 ms)
== D. documented silences must still time out ==
   RI    -> timeout as expected (212.49 ms)
   ZZZ   -> timeout as expected (207.77 ms)
   RPK9  -> timeout as expected (208.06 ms)
   left queued after the silences: 0
== E. input validation (no bytes on the wire) ==
   ''           rejected: ValueError
   'TOOLONGXX'  rejected: ValueError
   'PKé'        rejected: UnicodeEncodeError
== F. timeout floor rejected at construction ==
   rejected: timeout_ms=5 is below the 25 ms protocol floor
== G. actuate K0 and read back (DMM witnesses) ==
   start PK = 000
   set K0=1 -> RPK0='1'  ok
   set K0=0 -> RPK0='0'  ok
   set K0=1 -> RPK0='1'  ok
   set K0=0 -> RPK0='0'  ok
   MK000 (safe state)
   final PK = 000
== H. close is idempotent, does not raise ==
   is_open: False
   query after close: link is not open
== I. context manager ==
   inside : 000 is_open True
   after  : is_open False

ALL SECTIONS RAN

WHAT EACH SECTION ESTABLISHES
-----------------------------
A. Serial-based lookup works, and needs no device I/O at all: idVendor,
   idProduct, busnum, devnum and serial all come from sysfs. The path
   (001/015) is an OUTPUT of the lookup, never an input -- it changes on
   re-plug, which is why deploy/udev/63-benchctrl-adu218.rules deliberately
   offers no stable symlink.

B. open() -> CLAIMINTERFACE succeeded with nothing to detach, confirming on
   live hardware what hid_ignore_list predicts: usbhid sees an Ontrak vendor
   id and declines to bind. `is_open` False -> True -> False across the
   lifecycle. The drain reported 0 stale replies, i.e. the previous process
   (adu_latency.py, hours earlier) left the queue clean.

   Note the ioctl constants are COMPUTED here, from sizeof(struct
   usbdevfs_bulktransfer) = 24, and arrive at 0x8004550f / 0x80045510 /
   0xc0185502 -- byte-identical to the hardcoded values the probe scripts
   used successfully. Verified separately on the aarch64 host.

C. Every read answered on the first attempt, 12.93-16.25 ms. That sits inside
   the 16.68 ms worst case measured over 440 transfers in latency.txt and
   latency_after_command.txt, so DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 200 keeps its ~12x
   margin. WD=0 confirms the watchdog is disarmed, as the previous session
   left it.

D. THE IMPORTANT NEGATIVE RESULT. All three documented silences still time
   out at 200 ms (207.8-214.8 ms wall, i.e. the timeout plus ioctl overhead),
   and -- the part that would have broken the driver -- `drain()` afterwards
   reports **0 replies left queued**. A late reply arriving after the timeout
   would sit on EP 0x81 and be returned as the NEXT query's answer: a silent
   wrong value, not an error. It does not happen. Shortening 2000 ms to
   200 ms therefore does not convert an error into a stale success.

   `RI` is included as a command that does not exist, `ZZZ` as garbage, and
   `RPK9` as a VALID command with an out-of-range argument. All three are
   indistinguishable on the wire. That is why Adu218LinkTimeout is documented
   as ambiguous and why the per-command expectation lives in the driver.

E/F. Malformed commands are rejected before any byte reaches the device: an
   empty command, a 9-byte command (7 is the limit after the mandatory 0x01
   report id), and non-ASCII. And a sub-floor timeout is rejected at
   CONSTRUCTION, not at first use -- 5 ms is below the ~10-20 ms set by
   bInterval=10 at low speed, so it would fail CORRECT reads. Failing in the
   constructor means a bad config cannot reach the relays at all.

G. Four actuations of K0, device-reported read-back agreeing each time, and
   MK000 restoring 000. Necessary but NOT sufficient -- see the header, and
   see link_dmm_witness.txt for the second instrument.

H. close() is idempotent (called twice, no raise), and a query afterwards
   raises Adu218LinkError rather than operating on a closed fd. Note what
   close() does NOT do: it does not de-energise. Relays keep their state; the
   explicit way to drop them is MK000 / reset_relays(). Hiding a switching
   operation inside close() would make every teardown a bench event.

I. The context manager opens and closes, and `is_open` is False on exit even
   though the object outlives the block.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW
  - Nothing about the watchdog (WD stayed 0 throughout, deliberately: any
    command refeeds an armed timer, so a test that polls state would silently
    neuter the interlock it was trying to test).
  - Nothing about relays K1-K7 or any input port beyond a single RPA/RPB
    read; K0 is the only channel with a witness attached.
  - Nothing about contention. One process held the interface for the whole
    run. Whether a second CLAIMINTERFACE gets EBUSY is asserted in the code's
    error message but is UNTESTED on hardware.
  - No resistance claim. The ohm values in link_dmm_witness.txt are
    probe-path resistance; see on_resistance_drift.txt.
